- **Built:** **1867** (first lit the same year)
- **Structure:** 65-foot (19.8 m) wooden tapered tower, clad in white cedar shingles with a red lantern room. The station originally included a keeper's dwelling, fog alarm building, oil house, and boat shed.

- **Visiting:** Open seasonally (typically **May to October**). Offers guided tours, cultural events, photography opportunities, and coastal walking trails. Highly recommended for sunrise/sunset views and birdwatching.

| **Height** | ~34 ft (10 m) | ~65 ft (19.8 m) |
| **First Lit** | 1849 | 1867 |
| **Status** | Deactivated (1941), now private aid & museum | Active Coast Guard aid & heritage museum |
| **Environment** | Tidal Delaware Bay marsh | Exposed Atlantic/Northumberland Strait coast |
